AdaptMeasures.evidence_source: The purpose of the present study was to examine the predictive validity of mental toughness scores in the context of learning a complex task, specifically a complex computer game that involved strong cognitive and perceptual-motor demands. The predictive validity of a generic, trait-based measure was compared to that of a domain measure across a variety of cognitive, affective, and skill-based criteria, including a test of adaptive performance in which participants encountered unanticipated novel performance demands (Kraiger, Ford, & Salas, 1993). 'A test of adaptive performance' indicates an objective measure.

section_summary.extract_value: This introduction discusses mental toughness, its conceptual history, and the challenges in defining it. It highlights the lack of empirical research on its relationship with learning and performance outcomes. The present study aims to examine the predictive validity of trait-based versus domain-specific mental toughness in learning a complex computer game, including a test of adaptive performance, and its incremental validity beyond other predictors like ability, experience, self-efficacy, goal orientation, and core self-evaluations.
